flags.reason: The guide gives no avoidWhen guidance; left empty rather than guessed.

The guide's Sources note was checked on 17 October on 0.1.78-a116616, whose Table.tsx is identical to the installed dbe0e02, but the #264 fix in that build also stopped Text Appearance from reaching the table's own values: every string or number body cell is Coin Text given colour: bodyTextColor(modes), the tableHeader/label/color token, after Text's token colour (Table.tsx lines 108–110 and 143; Text.tsx line 153 puts style after the token colour), and that token is black in every mode, so Success, Warning, Error and the brand appearances set on the table leave the values black. Only Coin Text that a column renders itself still takes its own Text Appearance (or the table's, through the modes merged into it). The 17 October re-check measured Weight, JioPlus and the roles, not Text Appearance. This entry follows the installed package and leaves out the guide sentences it contradicts: Configuration's Status appearances card (“Success, Warning, and Error tint every body cell green, amber, or red; to mark one value, render your own cells.”), the Configuration description's “text size and the brand appearances are in the playground above”, the third Do & Don't pair (its Don't “Colour the whole table”: “Text appearance on the table tints every value, so nothing stands out.”), and the evidence's 12 October Text Appearance colours for body text. Guide fix #534 (Documentation, To do), filed by this run; it also asks Marcin whether black values under every Text Appearance are intended or a Component Bug. Re-extract once #534 is fixed and published. Added by Claude Code in the overnight run agentpack-batch12, for Marcin to confirm.

examples.purpose: Holdings on a portfolio screen, the guide's In context: a heading over a Table whose Change column renders Coin Text, green for gains and red for losses (the Text Appearance comes from each value, as the guide's Do “Colour single values” shows); pressing a row opens that holding, and the screen handles the press. The empty press handler stands for the screen's own navigation.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <Text>Your holdings</Text>
  <Table
    columns={[
      { key: 'asset', header: 'Asset' },
      { key: 'units', header: 'Units', align: 'right' },
      { key: 'value', header: 'Value', align: 'right' },
      {
        key: 'change',
        header: 'Change',
        align: 'right',
        render: (row) => (
          <Text modes={{ 'Text Appearance': row.change.startsWith('-') ? 'Error' : 'Success' }}>{row.change}</Text>
        ),
      },
    ]}
    data={[
      { asset: 'HDFC Bank', units: '120', value: '₹1,98,400', change: '+2.4%' },
      { asset: 'Reliance', units: '64', value: '₹1,52,900', change: '-0.8%' },
      { asset: 'Infosys', units: '210', value: '₹3,10,500', change: '+1.1%' },
      { asset: 'TCS', units: '48', value: '₹1,84,200', change: '+0.3%' },
    ]}
    onRowPress={(row) => {}}
  />
</VStack>

from.quote: The portfolio screen lists holdings with gains in green and losses in red. Pressing a row opens that holding; the screen handles the press.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions for the data-driven API.

props.name: data
props.description: An empty data array renders the header only; there is no empty state. Declared: Row records, one per table row.

props.name: children
props.description: Composition (Table.Header, Table.HeaderCell, Table.Body, Table.Row, Table.Cell): with children, columns, data and showHeader are ignored. Same look; a developer's choice, not a designer setting. Declared: Composition children (`Table.Header`, `Table.Body`, `Table.Row`, `Table.Cell`, `Table.HeaderCell`). When provided, `columns`/`data` are ignored and the children are rendered as-is. Maps to the Figma Slot.

props.name: showHeader
props.description: Show the header row in the data-driven API. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: getRowKey
props.description: Resolve a stable key per row. Defaults to the row index.

props.name: onRowPress
props.description: With onRowPress each row stays a row (role row), is focusable on the web, activates with Enter or Space, and fades to 60% while pressed. Declared: Called when a row is pressed (data-driven API). Makes rows pressable.

props.name: scrollable
props.description: Wraps the table in a horizontal scroller with the scrollbar hidden. Declared: Wrap the table in a horizontal `ScrollView`. Use with fixed-width columns for wide tables that exceed the viewport on mobile. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Scrolls the body under the header, which stays pinned vertically; with scrollable as well, the header scrolls sideways with the body. Declared: Cap the body height (px) and scroll rows vertically. The header stays pinned above the scroll region (data-driven and composition with `Table.Header`). Combine with `scrollable` for wide + tall tables on mobile.

props.name: columnWidth
props.description: A column's width beats columnWidth, which beats flex. Declared: Fixed width (px) applied to every column — header and body alike — so all columns share the same width. An explicit per-column `width` (on `TableColumn`, or on an individual `Table.Cell`/`Table.HeaderCell`) still takes precedence when set. Omit to let columns flex to share the available space.

props.name: trimOuterBorders
props.description: When `true`, the data-driven API hides the right divider on the last column and the bottom divider on the last row (flush outer edge). Figma draws dividers on every cell — leave this `false` (default) to match. Composition consumers can still set `isLastColumn` / `isLastRow` per cell. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessibility label for the table container.

props.name: modes
props.description: Design token modes for theming (e.g. `{ "Color Mode": "Light" }`).

props.name: Table.Header
props.description: A static sub-component of Table. Its own props: children, modes, style.

props.name: Table.HeaderCell
props.description: A static sub-component of Table. Its own props: children, align, width, flex, modes, style.

props.name: Table.Body
props.description: A static sub-component of Table. Its own props: children, modes, style.

props.name: Table.Row
props.description: A static sub-component of Table. Its own props: children, onPress, modes, style.

props.name: Table.Cell
props.description: A static sub-component of Table. Its own props: children, align, width, flex, isLastColumn, isLastRow, modes, style.

gaps.text: Figma's Table is one 720 × 190 component with one full-width header; in code each column has its own header cell, a line runs under the header, and rows are a little taller; widths, alignment, and scrolling exist only in code.
Figma rows are 38 px; the code's are about 42 px (body) and 45 px (header).
